name: Chicken and Potato Curry

ingredients.buy: 3 1/2 tbsp, deseeded and finely chopped (about 3 chiles)
6 cups, undrained (three and a half 14 oz cans)
3 1/2 cups (three and a half 13.5 fl oz cans)

Macros used in prose (500 cal, 42.4 g protein) are taken verbatim from the locked view; no numbers computed.

prose.intro_html:
Here is the honest truth about curry night. Most people think a good one comes from a jar or a takeout window, and both of those quietly empty your wallet while telling you that you could never make it yourself. That is a story, and it is not true. This chicken and potato curry is warm, spiced, and built for a full week of dinners, and it lands at 500 calories a serving with 42.4 grams of protein. That is real food doing real work.

What I love about this one is that it is patient food. You soften an onion, you wake up the spices in the pan, you let chicken and potatoes get to know each other in tomato and coconut. Nothing fancy, nothing you have to babysit. You do the work once and you eat well for days. That is the whole idea around here.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a pantry-spice curry, so most of the cost lives in the chicken and the two cans, and the rest is small aromatics you likely already own. A few notes to buy it clean:

  • Buy the whole boneless skinless chicken breast and cut the 1-inch pieces yourself. Pre-cut anything always costs more for the convenience, and cubing chicken takes about four minutes.
  • Coriander, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne are the backbone here. Ground jars keep for months in a cool cupboard, so this recipe uses down a supply you buy once and lean on for a dozen dinners.
  • Fresh ginger and fresh red chili go a long way. You only need a few tablespoons chopped, so grab a small knob of ginger and a couple of chiles rather than a big bag that goes soft in the drawer.
  • Coconut milk and diced tomatoes are the sauce. Full-fat coconut milk is what gives you that creamy top, so do not reach for the light can if you want the texture the recipe is built on.
  • Cilantro is the finish. A single bunch covers the chopped cup and a quarter you need at the end, with tender stems fine to chop right in.
prose.make_it:
This cooks in one large pan and it rewards a little patience up front. Do not rush the onion, that is where the sweetness comes from.

  1. Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 to 10 minutes until softened. Slow and low here, you want it soft and sweet, not browned hard.
  2. Add the garlic, ginger, and fresh red chili and cook another minute until fragrant. Your kitchen will tell you when it is ready.
  3. Stir in the ground coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and cayenne and cook one more minute, stirring so nothing scorches. Toasting the spices in the oil is what separates this from a bland pot.
  4. Add the tomato paste and stir well to combine, then add the chicken. Toss to coat it in the spices and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the chicken is sealed on the outside.
  5. Add the cubed potatoes, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and salt. Stir, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook 10 minutes or until the potatoes are fork-tender.
  6. Stir in the coconut milk and simmer one more minute until heated through. Taste and adjust the seasoning, stir in the fresh cilantro, and it is done.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers, and the trick to keeping them even is to weigh the pot. Cooking pulls water out of the sauce and adds it from the potatoes, so a scoop-by-eye method always shorts the last few boxes. Put your empty pan on a scale before you dish, then divide the finished weight by 14 and portion to that number. Every container lands the same, which is how each one holds its 500 calories and 42.4 grams of protein.

Give the sauce a stir between scoops so the coconut and tomato do not settle, and try to land a fair share of chicken and potato in each box. Cools and stacks in the fridge, and it reheats even better the next day once the spices have had a night to settle in.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is where the math earns its keep. Fourteen dinners out of one pan, spices you already stock, and two humble cans doing the heavy lifting on the sauce. This is what eating well on a budget actually looks like, warm curry that costs a fraction of the jar-and-takeout version and feeds you for most of a week.
prose.upsell_html: If a week of real dinners like this for the price of a couple of takeout orders sounds like your kind of math, that is the whole point of Thrifty Crew. head.description: A budget meal-prep chicken and potato curry that makes 14 servings at 500 calories and 42.4 grams of protein each. Warm spices, coconut, and one pan.

steps: Heat the coconut oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 to 10 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, ginger, and fresh red chili and cook another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the ground coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and cayenne pepper and cook a further minute, stirring occasionally.
Add the tomato paste and stir to combine, then add the chicken cubes and toss to coat in the spices, cooking 3 to 4 minutes until the chicken is sealed.
Add the cubed potatoes, diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and salt. Stir, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 10 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer another minute until heated through. Adjust the seasoning, stir in the fresh cilantro, and serve.
